Save the demonstration QMD in your course folder and open it in RStudio.

The examples use base R and require no downloaded data. Rendering also

than running R in your browser. If using the optional project file,
save it beside the QMD and open the project first.

## During the seminar

We will distinguish point probabilities, densities, and cumulative probabilities.
Integrals describe accumulated area, with geometry and R doing the calculations.
No hand evaluation of complicated integrals is needed.

We will examine normal CDFs, forecast probabilities, quantiles, and simulation.
A discrete vote-count model illustrates the normal approximation and continuity
correction. Bargaining and contract examples show how transformations change
the distribution of payoffs, and why a mean alone does not describe a decision.

## After class

Rerun the demonstrations and change one input at a time. Explain the difference
between a density height and an interval probability, and between changing
a forecast's standard deviation and increasing the number of simulated draws.

**B2 is due October 7 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific.** The instructions, prepared data,
and plotting helpers are in your private B2 repository. Submit the QMD and
current HTML there. Keep individual submissions private.
